summary: Use exact ranges in legacy Twin CI

delivery.outcome: The legacy Twin CI workflow validates the real exact event range on default-branch pushes, so material-delivery and adoption-sync checks observe the merged change instead of a synthetic ticket-only path
nonGoals: No Twin runtime, test or product-documentation change
No reusable new-project workflow, action revision or repository-ruleset change
No change to pull-request, review or manual-dispatch range semantics

architecture.decision: Use the immutable push event before SHA as the governance base on the default branch and apply the same fail-closed full-SHA validation already used for pull-request events
architecture.rollback: Revert the unmerged ticket commit; accepted base 50f2a8620db8e6ad6d0f76400699d122f8f0c084 remains unchanged

commands: Inspect the Linux event-range branch in .github/workflows/ci.yml
validation.evidence: A default-branch push resolves base from EVENT_BASE, validates a non-zero full SHA and invokes governance with exact base and head
